prompt:
You are an expert in Sanskrit grammar (vyakarana).

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): भल्लँ॒   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): परिभाषणहिंसादानेषु

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): उप + नि
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lun (aorist)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Prathama (third person)
- vacana (number): Eka (singular)
- dhatu_pada (ending set): Parasmaipada (active endings)

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): ह्रेषृँ॒   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): अव्यक्ते शब्दे

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): प्र + नि
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lun (aorist)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Prathama (third person)
- vacana (number): Bahu (plural)
- dhatu_pada (ending set): Parasmaipada (active endings)

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): णिविँ   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): सेवने सेचने संस्रने च

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): उप
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lun (aorist)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Madhyama (second person)
- vacana (number): Eka (singular)
- dhatu_pada (ending set): Parasmaipada (active endings)

verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).

gana (verb class): Tudadi (class 6)

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): नि
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative), followed by सन् (desiderative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lut (periphrastic future)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Uttama (first person)
- vacana (number): Eka (singular)

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): चरँ   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): गतौ भक्षणे च

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): none
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative), followed by सन् (desiderative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lut (periphrastic future)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Uttama (first person)
- vacana (number): Dvi (dual)

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): छ्यु॒ङ्   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): गतौ

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): उप
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative), followed by सन् (desiderative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): AshirLin (benedictive)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Madhyama (second person)
- vacana (number): Eka (singular)

Derive the requested conjugated verb form from the Sanskrit verbal root (dhatu, given in
Devanagari in its Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included), its
verb class (gana), its traditional meaning (artha), and the required
tense/mood (lakara), voice (prayoga), person (purusha), and number (vacana).
Each Sanskrit grammatical term is glossed in parentheses in English.

Write ONLY the final conjugated verb form, in Devanagari script, inside
<answer></answer> tags. If several forms are valid, give exactly one.
Do not include any text outside the answer tags.

=== Your task ===

dhatu (Sanskrit verbal root): खादृँ   (Dhatupatha citation form, anubandha markers included)
gana (verb class): Bhvadi (class 1)
artha (traditional meaning): भक्षणे

upasarga (Sanskrit verbal prefix): वि
sanadi (Sanskrit derived-root suffixes, innermost first): यङ् (intensive), followed by णिच् (causative), followed by सन् (desiderative)

Required form:
- lakara (tense/mood): Lit (perfect)
- prayoga (voice): Kartari (active)
- purusha (person): Madhyama (second person)
- vacana (number): Bahu (plural)
